title: Medical Case: Mrs. Patterson's Post-Op Heart Rupture
description: A post-operative cardiac emergency puts Meredith Grey and Preston Burke under scrutiny when heart surgery patient Mrs. Patterson suffers a rupture after surgery. Meredith fears she caused the injury during the operation, but the case evolves into an investigation of the true medical cause and the consequences of her delayed disclosure.
main_characters: Meredith Grey; Preston Burke; Mrs. Patterson
interfering_episode_characters: Richard Webber; Mr. Patterson; Nurse Tyler; George O'Malley; Cristina Yang; hospital lawyer
single_episode_progression_string: During Mrs. Patterson's heart surgery, Meredith nods off while holding the heart and later notices that her fingernail punctured her glove, leading her to fear she injured the patient. George reassures Meredith that the patient is probably fine, and Meredith delays telling Burke. Mrs. Patterson later develops swelling and sudden bleeding at the sternum, and Burke rushes her back to the OR. Meredith finally discloses the glove puncture. Burke finds a ventricular wall rupture far larger than a fingernail injury. Richard Webber orders chart copies and a legal review after speaking with Mr. Patterson. Meredith tries to explain Mrs. Patterson's abnormally thin heart walls to Mr. Patterson, who rejects the explanation. In the meeting with Richard and the hospital lawyer, Meredith admits she failed to report the possible contact immediately, and Burke helps establish that the rupture was caused by fragile heart tissue related to extreme weight loss rather than Meredith's fingernail.

title: Medical Case: Mrs. Drake's Retained Surgical Towel
description: Mrs. Drake's chronic breathing problems lead to surgery that uncovers a retained surgical towel from a prior operation, triggering a hospital-error investigation and forcing Preston Burke to confront his connection to the original case before ultimately apologizing to Mrs. Drake.
main_characters: Mrs. Drake; George O'Malley; Preston Burke
interfering_episode_characters: Richard Webber; Miranda Bailey; Cristina Yang
single_episode_progression_string: George reviews Mrs. Drake's scans, discusses her symptoms, and prepares her for surgery after learning she quit smoking years earlier and that her prior operation never felt right. During surgery, Richard Webber and Miranda Bailey discover a retained towel inside Mrs. Drake from the earlier procedure. Bailey assigns Cristina Yang to retrieve the records, and she finds that Preston Burke was the surgical fellow on the original case. George remains Mrs. Drake's main point of contact as she learns about the mistake. Bailey gives Burke the file. Burke later admits his past failure to report the retained towel and apologizes to Mrs. Drake.

title: Medical Case: Jerry Frost's Chronic Pain Reveals a Subdural Hemorrhage
description: Jerry Frost is admitted for severe chronic pain, but his addiction history causes skepticism about the legitimacy of his symptoms. When a violent collapse exposes a life-threatening brain bleed, the case forces the doctors to confront both emergency neurosurgical care and the dangers of bias in treating addicted patients.
main_characters: Jerry Frost; Derek Shepherd; Alex Karev
interfering_episode_characters: Izzie Stevens
single_episode_progression_string: Jerry Frost presents with chronic back pain and requests specific narcotics, leading Alex to dismiss him as drug-seeking while Derek insists his pain must still be treated seriously. Alex delays the ordered central line, and Derek later finds Jerry Frost in worsening distress. Derek and Alex confront Jerry Frost about his addiction and move to discharge him. Jerry Frost becomes agitated, falls, strikes his head, and loses consciousness. Derek reviews the CT with Alex and Izzie, identifies a subdural hemorrhage, and takes Jerry Frost to surgery with Alex and Izzie assisting. After the operation, Alex arranges a psychology consult to address Jerry Frost's addiction recovery.

title: Medical Case: Mr. Sterman's Post-Obstruction Recovery
description: Izzie Stevens manages Mr. Sterman's recovery after a bowel obstruction, monitoring the return of bowel function while their conversations reveal contrasting views about medicine, work, and personal life. The case resolves once his recovery milestones are finally met.
single_episode_progression_string: Izzie checks on Mr. Sterman's recovery, asking whether he is tolerating clear fluids, using the bathroom, and passing gas. Mr. Sterman falsely claims he has passed gas, then admits he is lying and reveals that he once attended medical school before leaving during clinical training. Their conversation turns to whether a doctor can balance career and family. Later, Mr. Sterman jokes that Izzie should invite him to the party if he poops. By the end of the episode, Mr. Sterman reports to Izzie that he has finally had a bowel movement.

title: Meredith Grey And Derek Shepherd's Secret Seattle Grace Romance Unravels Amid Professional Fallout And The Revelation Of Derek's Marriage
description: After a one-night stand, Meredith Grey discovers that Derek Shepherd is not just a romantic interest but a celebrated attending surgeon at Seattle Grace, turning their attraction into a secret and professionally risky relationship shaped by a steep power imbalance. As their romance deepens inside the hospital, Derek's authority over cases, careers, and operating room opportunities becomes entangled with his feelings for Meredith, raising concerns about favoritism, blurring the line between mentorship and intimacy, and fueling suspicion and jealousy among her peers. At the same time, Derek presents himself as a man who left New York behind without fully disclosing why he came to Seattle. Meredith struggles to prove herself on merit while investing emotionally in him, only for the relationship's hidden fault line to be exposed when Addison arrives and reveals that Derek is still married.
interfering_episode_characters: George O'Malley; Izzie Stevens; Cristina Yang; Miranda Bailey
single_episode_progression_string: Derek notices Meredith is off after surgery, asks how the case went, and later asks her to dinner. Meredith keeps him at a distance while dealing with exhaustion and guilt. Derek reveals he knows about the party at her house, showing how their private lives are bleeding into the hospital social circle. After the party spirals and Meredith comes home drunk, Derek waits outside for her. Meredith and Derek flirt, kiss, and have sex in his car. Bailey sees them together.

title: Meredith Grey Navigates Ellis Grey's Legacy At Home And At Seattle Grace Through Richard Webber's Influence
description: As Meredith Grey begins her surgical career at Seattle Grace, she struggles under the weight of being legendary surgeon Ellis Grey's daughter while privately caring for Ellis as Alzheimer's erases their shared history. Ellis's reputation shapes how Meredith is perceived at the hospital, and Richard Webber's long personal history with Ellis gives Meredith a distinct kind of attention from the Chief, tying her early career to family legacy, institutional authority, and unresolved personal familiarity. At the same time, Meredith's private life is defined by secrecy, caregiving, and unresolved pain in her relationship with Ellis, making her mother's history an inescapable force in both her personal and professional world.
main_characters: Meredith Grey; Ellis Grey; Richard Webber
interfering_episode_characters: Nursing home representative; Notary's secretary; Nursing home doctor; Preston Burke; hospital lawyer
single_episode_progression_string: Meredith goes to Ellis's nursing home to discuss signing over Ellis's estate, finances, and medical care while Ellis is lucid. A nursing home representative pressures Meredith to handle the decisions herself. Meredith arranges for a notary and the home's doctor to witness the signing. When Meredith brings Ellis in to sign, Ellis is in the middle of an Alzheimer's episode, refuses to sign, and cannot complete the process. The notary's secretary halts the signing and tells Meredith to return when Ellis is lucid. Later, Richard Webber directly intervenes in Meredith's professional crisis over Mrs. Patterson and presides over the meeting that determines her status. By the end of the episode, Ellis is lucid enough to sign the documents in front of Meredith.

title: Meredith Grey And Cristina Yang Build A Friendship Through Rivalry
description: Meredith and Cristina form a defining intern friendship built on mutual respect, sharp honesty, and relentless competition. They gravitate toward each other because they recognize the same ambition and detachment in one another, but their bond is repeatedly tested when professional opportunities, personal secrets, and perceived favoritism put them on opposite sides. Over time, they become each other's most important ally while continuing to compete for status, cases, and surgical recognition.
interfering_episode_characters: George O'Malley; Preston Burke; Richard Webber; Izzie Stevens
single_episode_progression_string: Cristina reacts with jealousy that Meredith got to hold a heart in Burke's surgery and dismisses the task as something a monkey could do. Later, Meredith confides to Cristina and George that she may have damaged Mrs. Patterson's heart and fears being thrown out of the program. Cristina responds with blunt pragmatism and questions why Meredith told Burke. At the party, Meredith and Cristina get drunk and dance together. After Meredith survives the meeting with the chief, the episode ends with Meredith and Cristina cleaning the house together.

title: Meredith Decides To Keep Ellis Grey's House And Open It To George And Izzie
description: Meredith's inherited family home shifts from a house she plans to sell into a shared refuge for herself and fellow interns George O'Malley and Izzie Stevens. As their medical careers and personal lives intensify, the house becomes the foundation of their found-family dynamic.
main_characters: Meredith Grey; George O'Malley; Izzie Stevens; Ellis Grey
interfering_episode_characters: Cristina Yang; Miranda Bailey; Notary's secretary; Hank
single_episode_progression_string: Meredith arranges for Ellis to sign house-related documents, but the effort initially fails when Ellis is not lucid enough to complete the signing. Meanwhile, Izzie plans a gathering at Meredith's house and expands it far beyond the small event Meredith expected, while George repeatedly warns that Meredith has not approved this. Bailey learns about the party and George ends up including her as well. Meredith returns home to find the house overtaken by a large party and confronts George about it. By the next morning, Meredith, George, Izzie, and Cristina are cleaning up together, and later Ellis signs the documents.

title: Cristina Yang And Preston Burke's Professional Orbit Begins
description: Cristina Yang's intense focus on surgery draws her repeatedly into Preston Burke's orbit, where professional ambition, competition, and mutual respect begin to form the basis of a deeper connection. As their dynamic develops, professional opportunity, rivalry, and emotional intimacy become increasingly entangled.
interfering_episode_characters: Miranda Bailey; Mrs. Drake; Richard Webber
single_episode_progression_string: Cristina watches Burke's heart surgery from the gallery and reacts to being excluded from the case. Burke later brings Cristina coffee, creating an awkward private moment. Cristina discovers Burke's name in Mrs. Drake's old surgical file and brings the information to Bailey. Cristina and Burke then share another guarded exchange about the heart graft complication. Bailey later tells Cristina that Burke had already intended to reveal the truth when the time was right. By the end of the episode, Cristina and Burke have sex in the locker room.

title: Izzie Stevens And Alex Karev's Public Humiliation Rivalry
description: Izzie and Alex sustain a hostile peer dynamic marked by ridicule, status games, and personal attacks. Alex repeatedly singles Izzie out and tries to reduce her to her modeling past, while Izzie refuses to be shamed and answers his cruelty directly. Their conflict becomes a recurring intern rivalry built on humiliation, defiance, and escalating antagonism.
interfering_episode_characters: Derek Shepherd; Hank; Jerry Frost; George O'Malley; Cristina Yang
single_episode_progression_string: Alex asks about the party and Izzie joins George and Cristina in denying it. Later, Alex needles Izzie while she orders beer and asks for local microbrews and bar nuts. In the hallway, Alex provocatively tells Izzie to ask Hank to get the beers, and Izzie snaps that she did not invite Alex because he is unpleasant. Their conflict is redirected when Derek pulls both of them onto Jerry Frost's emergency case, where they assist together in surgery.

title: Izzie Stevens And Hank Grow Apart As Medicine Takes Over Her Life
description: Izzie's relationship with Hank deteriorates as her identity as a doctor reshapes her priorities, schedule, and sense of self. What once fit her old life no longer fits the demands of surgical training, and Hank struggles to accept how completely medicine now defines her time and commitments.
interfering_episode_characters: George O'Malley; Cristina Yang; Meredith Grey; Mr. Sterman; Alex Karev; Derek Shepherd; Jerry Frost
single_episode_progression_string: Izzie plans a party so Hank can meet her hospital friends, despite George and Cristina questioning the idea and whether Meredith approved it. While caring for Mr. Sterman, Izzie insists that a person can have both a successful career and a family. But when Jerry Frost's crisis escalates, Izzie stays at the hospital for emergency surgery instead of going to the party. Hank arrives to find Izzie absent, then later confronts her outside the hospital. He rejects the party and the idea of meeting her coworkers, while Izzie explains that her life has changed and her patients come first. Hank leaves.

title: Meredith, George, Izzie, and Cristina Turn Meredith's House into a Dysfunctional Intern Home
description: As internship consumes their lives, Meredith, George, Izzie, and Cristina form an unstable but lasting bond that extends beyond the hospital. Living in and around Meredith's home, they clash over boundaries, create personal chaos for one another, and repeatedly regroup afterward, slowly becoming a dysfunctional found family.
main_characters: Meredith Grey; George O'Malley; Izzie Stevens; Cristina Yang
interfering_episode_characters: Miranda Bailey; Alex Karev; Derek Shepherd; Hank
single_episode_progression_string: Izzie expands Meredith's intended small gathering into a full party at Meredith's house without permission. George and Cristina object as the guest list keeps growing, and George accidentally ends up inviting Bailey when she overhears. Meredith returns home to find the party already underway, is overwhelmed, but instead of shutting it down joins George and Cristina in drinking and dancing. By the next morning, Meredith, George, Izzie, and Cristina are back together in the wrecked house, dealing with the aftermath and cleaning up as a unit.

title: Izzie Stevens Fights To Be Taken Seriously As A New Intern
description: Izzie Stevens begins her surgical internship already marked by others' assumptions about her looks and background. Across the season, she struggles to earn professional respect, takes on humiliating or low-status tasks, and repeatedly has to prove that she belongs in medicine. Her early insecurity and inexperience shape her interactions with supervisors and peers as she tries to establish herself as a capable doctor.
interfering_episode_characters: Mr. Sterman; Hank; Derek Shepherd; Jerry Frost; Alex Karev
single_episode_progression_string: In her conversation with Mr. Sterman, Izzie pushes back on the idea that a doctor cannot have both a career and a family. She continues managing his recovery and stays engaged in patient care. When Jerry Frost's condition turns critical, Izzie chooses to remain at the hospital for emergency surgery instead of leaving for the party. Later, she tells Hank that her life has changed and that her patients come first.

title: George O'Malley's Fight For Confidence And Respect
description: George O'Malley begins his surgical internship as the least assured of his class and is quickly marked as an easy target for doubt and ridicule. Across the season, he struggles to earn respect from attendings, peers, and himself after early mistakes damage his confidence. His arc follows a difficult climb from humiliation and second-guessing toward professional steadiness, as his compassion with patients and refusal to quit gradually establish that he belongs in the program.
interfering_episode_characters: Mrs. Drake; Miranda Bailey; Richard Webber; Meredith Grey
single_episode_progression_string: Bailey and Webber have George assess Mrs. Drake's films, and George correctly identifies the lung problems and proposes a bullectomy. George explains the procedure to Mrs. Drake, initially makes a wrong assumption about her smoking, then regains trust through honesty and bedside manner. After the retained towel is discovered, Bailey assigns George to stay with Mrs. Drake because she likes him. George also serves as a sounding board for Meredith during the heart complication.

title: Meredith Grey Begins Her Surgical Career While Proving Her Identity And Talent Are Her Own
description: In her first year at Seattle Grace, Meredith Grey begins the difficult transition from emotional detachment into adult responsibility as she starts life as a surgeon. Working under intense pressure, she must prove herself in high-stakes cases while living in the shadow of Ellis Grey's legendary reputation and coping with Ellis's worsening condition. At the same time, her personal involvement with Derek Shepherd complicates her professional standing, leading others to question whether her opportunities and successes come from merit, legacy, or favoritism. As Meredith demonstrates strong instincts, resilience, and growing skill, she gradually learns painful lessons about competence, death, accountability, and self-definition.
interfering_episode_characters: Preston Burke; George O'Malley; Richard Webber; hospital lawyer; Mr. Patterson; Nurse Tyler; Ellis Grey; Nursing home representative; Derek Shepherd; Cristina Yang; Izzie Stevens
single_episode_progression_string: Meredith juggles Ellis Grey's legal and medical affairs before surgery and arrives exhausted for a major cardiac case. While assisting Burke, Meredith briefly falls asleep holding Mrs. Patterson's heart and later discovers her glove was punctured, leading her to fear she caused damage. After George reassures her, she delays reporting it. Mrs. Patterson crashes, and Meredith finally tells Burke as the patient is rushed back to the OR. Burke discovers a ventricular rupture larger than a fingernail puncture, but Meredith still faces scrutiny for failing to report the possible mistake immediately. Meredith reviews the case, realizes the patient's dramatic weight loss may have weakened the heart wall, and presents that explanation in the meeting with Webber and the hospital lawyer. Burke backs her by admitting his own past error. Meredith avoids dismissal but is placed under observation.

title: Seattle Grace Interns Endure Their First Year Of Surgical Training
description: Meredith Grey, Cristina Yang, George O'Malley, Izzie Stevens, and Alex Karev begin their careers at Seattle Grace as inexperienced surgical interns and are immediately thrown into an unforgiving training system. From their first day, they face grueling hours, public mistakes, humiliations, harsh supervision, competitive assignments, and constant exposure to life-and-death patient care. Across the season, their professional arc follows their struggle to survive the program, function under pressure, earn credibility, learn from mistakes, and grow from overwhelmed interns into real surgeons capable of handling the hospital's demanding culture.
main_characters: Meredith Grey; Cristina Yang; George O'Malley; Izzie Stevens; Alex Karev
interfering_episode_characters: Preston Burke; Miranda Bailey; Richard Webber; Derek Shepherd; Mrs. Patterson; Mr. Patterson; Mrs. Drake; Jerry Frost; hospital lawyer; Nurse Tyler; Ellis Grey; Hank
single_episode_progression_string: Meredith is exhausted after 48 hours without sleep, nods off while assisting in heart surgery, fears she damaged the patient, and then has to face Burke, Webber, and legal scrutiny when Mrs. Patterson crashes. George is tested on Mrs. Drake's case, learns from Richard and Bailey, and stays involved as the team uncovers a towel left from a prior surgery. Cristina competes for surgical standing, investigates the old case files, and becomes entangled in the professional consequences surrounding Burke. Alex is corrected by Derek for dismissing a pain patient as a drug seeker and is forced to learn a more responsible standard of care. Izzie chooses surgery and patient care over Hank and the party.

title: Miranda Bailey's Intimidating Surgical Training Of The Interns
description: Miranda Bailey oversees the interns with strict discipline, blunt authority, and little patience for weakness. She sets the tone of their surgical education by assigning work, enforcing rules, correcting mistakes, and making clear that competence must be earned. Her mentorship is severe and often humiliating, but it defines the standards the interns must survive and meet as they begin their training.
interfering_episode_characters: George O'Malley; Cristina Yang; Richard Webber; Preston Burke; Mrs. Drake
single_episode_progression_string: Bailey quizzes George on Mrs. Drake's chest films and asks him to state the diagnosis and treatment plan. She assists Richard during Mrs. Drake's surgery when a retained towel is discovered, then immediately assigns Cristina to investigate the original operation and orders George to remain with Mrs. Drake. Bailey tells Cristina to keep the information quiet while the attendings handle it. She also reveals she knows about the interns' party and puts George on the spot. Later, Bailey gives Burke the file from the earlier surgery and tells Cristina that Burke had already intended to come forward.

title: The Interns Compete For Surgeries, Status, And Survival
description: The surgical interns enter a training culture where access to procedures, recognition, and advancement must be earned through performance under pressure. Attendings and residents control opportunities, mistakes carry immediate consequences, and every case becomes a test of skill, nerve, and standing among peers. Competition for surgeries and approval shapes the interns' reputations, alliances, and rivalries.
main_characters: Meredith Grey; Cristina Yang; George O'Malley; Alex Karev
interfering_episode_characters: Preston Burke; Miranda Bailey; Richard Webber; Derek Shepherd; hospital lawyer; Ellis Grey; Mrs. Patterson; Mrs. Drake
single_episode_progression_string: Meredith gets a coveted opportunity to assist Burke and hold a heart during surgery, prompting jealousy from George and Cristina. George is tested on Mrs. Drake's case by Bailey and Webber and is assigned to guide her through treatment, while Cristina is tasked with digging through records tied to the earlier surgical error. Alex is challenged by Derek after dismissing a pain patient as drug-seeking. Meredith realizes she may have damaged Mrs. Patterson's heart after dozing in surgery and hiding a torn glove, then faces the consequences when the patient crashes. Webber and the hospital lawyer review the case as a threat to her future in the program. In the end, Burke admits his own past failure to report a surgical mistake, helping spare Meredith from dismissal, though she is placed under observation for a month.

title: Cristina Yang's Competitive Pursuit Of Surgical Opportunity
description: Cristina treats surgical training as a constant competition where skill, speed, and access to the operating room determine worth. She pushes for difficult cases, dismisses distractions, and measures herself against the people around her. As the internship progresses, her intense focus on surgical advancement repeatedly collides with friendship, hierarchy, and the emotional realities of patient care.
interfering_episode_characters: Preston Burke; Meredith Grey; Izzie Stevens; Miranda Bailey; Richard Webber
single_episode_progression_string: Cristina is angry that Burke did not choose her to assist in surgery and dismisses Izzie's party plans as a waste of time compared with serious surgical work. Burke unexpectedly brings Cristina coffee. Bailey assigns Cristina to investigate Mrs. Drake's old surgical records, and Cristina discovers that Burke was the fellow on the operation where the towel was left behind. She quietly brings that information to Bailey, later probes Burke about Mrs. Patterson's complication, and studies his reaction. When Cristina sees Bailey hand Burke the file, she realizes his direct connection to the retained towel case.

title: Alex Karev's Arrogance Sabotages His Standing As An Intern
description: Alex Karev moves through the program with confidence that often hardens into arrogance, impatience, and open contempt for coworkers and patients. Across the arc, his dismissive behavior and snap judgments repeatedly damage his credibility, isolate him from the people around him, and interfere with his growth as a surgeon.
interfering_episode_characters: Derek Shepherd; Jerry Frost; Izzie Stevens
single_episode_progression_string: Alex immediately labels Jerry Frost a junkie, dismisses his pain as fake, and argues against treating him properly despite Derek's warning to err on the side of caution. Derek later berates Alex for his judgmental attitude and points out that Alex only sees an addict instead of a patient with real pain. Alex also needles Izzie about the party and remains abrasive with the others. After Jerry's collapse, Alex assists in surgery and later arranges follow-up care.

title: Preston Burke's Surgical Authority Is Tested by a Current Cardiac Complication and the Exposure of His Past Retained-Sponge Error
description: Preston Burke's authority as an elite cardiothoracic surgeon is challenged when a postoperative crisis, intern error, legal scrutiny, and the resurfacing of his own past surgical mistake force him to balance leadership, accountability, and professional self-preservation within Seattle Grace's hierarchy.
interfering_episode_characters: Meredith Grey; Miranda Bailey; Cristina Yang; Mrs. Patterson; Mr. Patterson; Mrs. Drake; hospital lawyer
single_episode_progression_string: Burke leads Mrs. Patterson's heart surgery and notices Meredith drifting while assisting. When Mrs. Patterson deteriorates post-op, Burke rushes her back to surgery, where Meredith admits she tore her glove during the first operation. Burke reprimands her for withholding that information, then discovers a ventricular wall rupture larger than any fingernail puncture. Richard orders Burke to submit charts and face legal review. Meanwhile, Bailey and Cristina investigate Mrs. Drake's earlier surgery and uncover that Burke was the fellow on the case where a towel was left inside the patient. Bailey gives Burke the file. At the meeting with Richard and the hospital lawyer, Burke defends Meredith by confessing his own role in the earlier retained-sponge case. Burke later apologizes to Mrs. Drake.

title: Seattle Grace's Chain Of Command And Competitive Training Culture
description: Seattle Grace operates through a strict medical hierarchy where the Chief, attendings, residents, and interns enforce status through assignments, discipline, public correction, and selective opportunity. As the interns begin their training, they must navigate intimidation, favoritism, competition for surgeries, and the career consequences of mistakes. The hospital's culture teaches them that medical skill alone is not enough; survival also depends on reading power, earning trust, and enduring humiliation inside the system.
main_characters: Meredith Grey; Preston Burke; Richard Webber; Miranda Bailey
interfering_episode_characters: Cristina Yang; George O'Malley; hospital lawyer; Mrs. Patterson; Mr. Patterson; Mrs. Drake; Derek Shepherd; Alex Karev
single_episode_progression_string: Burke gives Meredith a prized role in Mrs. Patterson's heart surgery, and George and Cristina react with jealousy over the opportunity. Bailey quizzes George on Mrs. Drake's case, assigns Cristina to dig through old files, and orders George to stay with the patient. Derek publicly corrects Alex for judging Jerry Frost instead of following instructions. When Mrs. Patterson crashes post-op, Meredith finally tells Burke about the torn glove, and Burke harshly reprimands her. Richard escalates the matter into a formal review with legal, making Meredith's future in the program uncertain. In parallel, Bailey's investigation into Mrs. Drake's retained towel case connects Burke to the earlier surgery. At Meredith's disciplinary meeting, the hospital lawyer presses the liability issue, and Burke publicly admits his own past failure to report the Drake error.

title: The Surgical Interns Learn Through Errors, Pressure, And First Life-Or-Death Cases
description: The new surgical interns are initiated into hospital life through hierarchy, humiliation, technical mistakes, emergency judgment calls, and the emotional burden of patient outcomes. Meredith Grey, Cristina Yang, George O'Malley, Izzie Stevens, and Alex Karev learn that becoming surgeons requires not just intelligence, but resilience, accountability, and the ability to function under intense pressure as they move from students toward doctors.
main_characters: Meredith Grey; George O'Malley; Izzie Stevens; Cristina Yang; Alex Karev
interfering_episode_characters: Preston Burke; Derek Shepherd; Miranda Bailey; Richard Webber; Mrs. Patterson; Mr. Patterson; Mrs. Drake; Jerry Frost; Nurse Tyler; hospital lawyer
single_episode_progression_string: Meredith falls asleep while assisting in Burke's heart surgery and later fears she damaged Mrs. Patterson's heart, but delays reporting the torn glove until the patient crashes. George helps manage Mrs. Drake's case, which reveals a towel left behind from an earlier surgery, while Cristina uncovers Burke's connection to that past mistake. Alex is forced by Derek to confront his bias against Jerry Frost's addiction and participate in emergency surgery after Jerry collapses. Izzie remains engaged in patient care and emergency surgery as the interns continue learning under pressure. Meredith ultimately faces formal review, explains the medical factors behind Mrs. Patterson's rupture, and is spared dismissal when Burke admits his own past failure.

title: Derek Shepherd Pushes Alex Karev To Treat Addicted Patients As Real Patients
description: Derek's supervision of Alex repeatedly tests Alex's tendency to judge difficult patients before fully treating them. Across the season, Derek challenges Alex's reflexive cynicism and pushes him to separate addiction, attitude, and appearance from actual medical need. Their mentor-trainee dynamic centers on whether Alex can develop the discipline, compassion, and clinical judgment required to care for vulnerable patients without reducing them to labels.
interfering_episode_characters: Jerry Frost; Izzie Stevens
single_episode_progression_string: Alex dismisses Jerry Frost as a drug seeker and wants to discharge him. Derek insists that Jerry's pain must be treated as real, orders Alex to place a central line, and later reprimands him for letting judgment interfere with care. When Jerry tries to leave, falls, and suffers a subdural hemorrhage, Derek brings Alex into the emergency surgery. During the operation, Alex reveals his father was addicted to heroin. Afterward, Alex takes a more responsible approach by arranging psychological follow-up for Jerry.
